public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 314

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/

@[expose] public section


namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture314

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]

/-- The size of a largest induced path of $G$, as a natural number.

A subset $s \subseteq V(G)$ is an *induced path* when the induced subgraph
`G.induce s` is a tree in which every vertex has degree at most $2$
(equivalently: a tree that is itself a path graph). We define
`largestInducedPathSize G` as the supremum of `s.card` over all such subsets.

**Disambiguation.** This is *not* the `SimpleGraph.path` invariant, which is the
floor of the average distance — that one is the wrong tool for WOWII Conjecture
314, where $\mathrm{path}(G)$ denotes the **size of a largest induced path**.

TODO: it would probably be clearer to rename the `SimpleGraph.path` invariant to
something like `pathBound` / `floorAvgDist` to avoid this naming collision. -/
noncomputable def largestInducedPathSize (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : ℕ :=
  sSup { n | ∃ s : Finset α,
              s.card = n ∧
              (G.induce (s : Set α)).IsTree ∧
              ∀ v : (s : Set α), (G.induce (s : Set α)).degree v ≤ 2 }

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 314](http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html#conj314):

For every finite simple connected graph $G$ with $n > 1$ vertices,
if $G$ is triangle-free and $\mathrm{path}(G) \le 4$, then $G$ is well totally
dominated.

Here $\mathrm{path}(G) = \mathrm{largestInducedPathSize}\, G$ is the **size of a
largest induced path** in $G$, defined locally above.

**Disambiguation.** Earlier revisions of this file used the `SimpleGraph.path`
invariant, but that is the *floor of the average distance*, not the size of a
largest induced path — a different quantity that makes Conjecture 314 vacuous
in many cases.

**Proof summary.** In a connected, $K_{3}$-free, induced-$P_{5}$-free graph $G$:

1. No minimal total dominating set has fewer than two vertices.
2. No minimal total dominating set has more than three vertices.
3. Minimal total dominating sets of sizes two and three cannot coexist.

Thus, each minimal total dominating set in $G$ has the same size.

The Lean proof was generated by OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/glyaea/wow-ii-314/blob/7b35f1252e4aaae3c787faf8091f9c7cd4edc41f/solution.lean"]
theorem conjecture314 [Nontrivial α] (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hG : G.Connected)
    (hTriFree : ∀ a b c : α, G.Adj a b → G.Adj b c → G.Adj c a → False)
    (hPath : largestInducedPathSize G ≤ 4) :
    IsWellTotallyDominated G := by
  sorry

-- Sanity checks

/-- The complete graph $K_3$ has a triangle. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example : ∃ a b c : Fin 3, (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)).Adj a b ∧
    (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)).Adj b c ∧ (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)).Adj c a := by
  exact ⟨0, 1, 2, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩

/-- `largestInducedPathSize G` is nonneg. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) [DecidableRel G.Adj] :
    0 ≤ largestInducedPathSize G := Nat.zero_le _

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture314

findings.description: The disambiguation at lines 43–48 incorrectly says that `SimpleGraph.path` is the floor of average distance and is a different invariant. At this commit, `SimpleGraph.path` already maximizes the number of vertices of an induced path, using `isInducedPath`. It is equivalent to the local definition on finite graphs. The proposed rename to `floorAvgDist` is consequently obsolete. The local definition itself is mathematically correct.
findings.source_evidence: WOWII's glossary, entry 35, defines path(G) as “The number of vertices of a largest induced path of the graph” (http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/wowIIdefs.js, read through the archived capture listed below). At the reviewed commit, FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/VertexDistance.lean:45–54 implements precisely this invariant as `SimpleGraph.path`; this was also confirmed with `#print`.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the obsolete disambiguation and renaming TODO, or explain that the local tree-and-degree characterization gives the same invariant as the current `SimpleGraph.path`. No mathematical statement needs changing.

findings.description: The theorem's disambiguation at lines 65–68 repeats the obsolete present-tense assertion that `SimpleGraph.path` is floor-average-distance rather than largest induced-path size. Whatever earlier implementations did, this is false of the imported definition at the reviewed commit. The theorem itself faithfully states Conjecture 314.
findings.source_evidence: Conjecture 314 requires a triangle-free simple connected graph with n > 1 and path number ≤ 4. Glossary entry 35 defines path number by the number of vertices in a largest induced path. The current `SimpleGraph.path` in FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/VertexDistance.lean:45–54 already has that meaning.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete this paragraph, or explicitly describe the floor-average-distance implementation as historical and acknowledge that the current shared definition has been corrected.

reformulations.difference: The source defines path number as the number of vertices in a largest induced path. Lean takes a natural-number supremum over vertex subsets whose induced graphs are trees with every degree at most two.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A finite nonempty tree of maximum degree at most two is a path graph, and every nonempty path graph satisfies those conditions. Thus the admissible subsets are exactly the nonempty induced paths. Their cardinalities are bounded by the graph's number of vertices, so the supremum is their maximum. Singletons supply witnesses in nonempty graphs; the empty graph gives zero. The boundedness, supremum-to-finite-maximum conversion, and small cases were checked in Lean, but the full equivalence with ordered induced paths was not formally proved.

reformulations.difference: The source says every minimal total dominating set is a minimum total dominating set. The Lean conclusion says all inclusion-minimal total dominating sets have equal cardinality.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every finite total dominating set T contains an inclusion-minimal total dominating subset U. If all minimal sets have equal size, any minimal S satisfies |S| = |U| ≤ |T|, so S is minimum. Conversely, any two minimum sets have equal cardinality. This exact equivalence was proved in `/workspace/review/scratch.lean` as `Review314.well_total_iff_every_minimal_is_minimum`, with only standard axioms.

review.notes: No substantive misformalization was found; both anonymous sanity checks are also correct. Finiteness and Nontrivial match the source's domain, and connectedness with Nontrivial ensures total dominating sets exist. Lean checks established the supremum bound and tested empty/singleton graphs, K2, K3, paths through six vertices, C4 and C5. P5 has minimal total dominating sets of sizes 3 and 4 and is correctly excluded by the path bound. The July 2026 source snapshot still displays O, but the cited external proof was independently compiled after updating its old import path. A separately namespaced copy directly proves the exact repository statement; `#print axioms` reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Thus the research solved and formal_proof records are substantiated, not stale. Experiments are in `/workspace/review/scratch.lean` and `/workspace/review/linked_proof_bridge.lean`.
